comparisons.peer_topic: Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) Requirements and Compliance
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation must maintain a minimum SLR of 3.0% plus a 2.0% leverage buffer to avoid restrictions on capital distributions and bonus payments, with the numerator defined as quarter-end Basel 3 Tier 1 capital and the denominator based on total leverage exposure. At December 31, 2024, its insured depository institution subsidiaries exceeded the 6.0% minimum SLR required to be considered well capitalized under the PCA framework.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America define the Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) using the same regulatory framework components: Tier 1 capital as the numerator and total leverage exposure as the denominator. Both explicitly state the minimum requirement of 3.0% for Basel III Advanced approach organizations and the additional 2.0% leverage buffer required for systemic firms. JPMorgan defines total leverage exposure as average on-balance sheet assets (net of deductions) plus off-balance sheet exposures. Bank of America aligns on the numerator (quarter-end Basel 3 Tier 1 capital) and denominator structure (daily average on-balance sheet exposures less deductions and average off-balance sheet exposures), confirming the identical calculation methodology and regulatory minima.

sentences.text: Banking organizations subject to the Basel III Advanced approach are currently required to have a minimum SLR of 3.0%.
Certain banking organizations, including the Firm, are also required to hold an additional 2.0% leverage buffer.
The SLR is defined as Tier 1 capital under Basel III divided by the Firm's total leverage exposure.

Total leverage exposure is calculated by taking the Firm's total average on-balance sheet assets, less amounts permitted to be deducted for Tier 1 capital, and adding certain off-balance sheet exposures, as defined in regulatory capital rules.

The Corporation is also required to maintain a minimum supplementary leverage ratio (SLR) of 3.0 percent plus a leverage buffer of 2.0 percent in order to avoid certain restrictions on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments to executive officers.
The numerator of the SLR is quarter-end Basel 3 Tier 1 capital.

The denominator is total leverage exposure based on the daily average of the sum of on-balance sheet exposures less permitted deductions and the simple average of certain off-balance sheet exposures, as of the end of each month in a quarter.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup's Supplementary Leverage Ratio was 5.8% as of December 31, 2024, largely unchanged from the prior year, as higher Tier 1 Capital was offset by an increase in Total Leverage Exposure.
comparisons.comparison: Citigroup reports its actual Supplementary Leverage Ratio (5.8%), while JPMorgan defines the metric and its regulatory floor. Both disclosures identify the same core components of the SLR: Tier 1 Capital and Total Leverage Exposure. Citigroup notes that its ratio remained unchanged from the prior year because higher Tier 1 Capital was offset by an increase in Total Leverage Exposure, directly mirroring the structural definition provided by JPMorgan where SLR is Tier 1 capital divided by total leverage exposure. This indicates a consistent industry application of the same two key financial drivers to the ratio.
